newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican prisons head sees mine shafts as jails.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican prisons head sees mine shafts as jails.

text.p: Violent criminals should be jailed in old mine shafts never to see daylight again, South Africa's prisons commissioner said on Tuesday.

"They (serious criminals) are animals that must never see sunlight again," Correctional Services Department Commissioner Khulekani Sitole said in a statement, adding that a probe was considering the possibility of transforming disused shafts into maximum-security jails.
"There are criminals within our system who have made it clear that they are not prepared to conform to the norms of a democratic society."
Violent crime is at relatively high levels in South Africa, although statistics released on Tuesday showed that murders, "carjacking" and drug-related crime had declined in 1996 from 1995 figures.
But the minister in charge of police, Sydney Mufamadi, said: "Crime levels in South Africa remain unacceptably high."
Sitole added he knew he would be criticised by human rights activists for the suggestion.
"I am fully aware that human rights is an important issue in this new democracy, but we also have to consider the rights of society in whose service we stand."
He said mine shaft jails would alleviate overcrowding in existing prisons and prevent escapes.
